summary: New mission publication supersedes already-active stale runs by default, without overriding existing revision policies. Human-only missions keep person-reviewed proposals; approved cutover creates a fresh linked run at the exact approved revision. When-idle missions wait for their next idle boundary. Replacement admission precedes cancellation; fresh runs retain exact inputs and workspace, wait for ordinary cleanup, and restart every step and program without journal adoption. Incompatible sources remain active with a visible fault. Native and public readers expose supersession lineage alongside retry links.

replay.detail: Append-only mission-run.supersede-linked claims restore both lineage endpoints; reconcile.fault claims in scope mission/supersession restore admission refusals and recovery. Unprotected publication or authorized approved cutover creates a fresh replacement and ordinarily cancels its source atomically only after start admission succeeds. Existing review authorization, exact preview binding, approval recovery, and accepted timestamps remain authoritative. Automatic idle holds reuse canonical revision-draining state and existing work-holder completion; refusal releases the hold. A rebuildable member-local queue observes selected heads, including delayed owned-set promotion. Replacement deadlines start at cleanup admission or retained after-run dependency admission, using accepted timestamps on replay.

schema.detail: Register system-only mission-run.supersede-linked with source/replacement references and publication string. Extend mission-run.created with optional phase/admission_publication and reconcile.fault with optional publication. Reuse revision-draining; replacements use supersession-waiting. Full evaluation/reconciliation views hydrate execution lineage, not just presentation views; cheap headers remain separate. Install private rebuildable v3 head cursors and indexed mission_run_capacity_v1 facts/totals. Malformed or excessively deep JSON, non-object bodies, missing revisions, and invalid limits project to refusal without aborting canonical source writes or becoming unlimited. Bootstrap, counters, and witnesses commit together; complete reopen does not write. Disposable projections are not replicated authority or shared digests. Views gain optional non-null supersedes, superseded_by, and supersession_fault, retaining retry fields and older-response decoding. No destructive rewrite.

rules.detail: Registry and retention compatibility digests change for supersession contracts. Existing human-review and idle-cutover policies take precedence; publication cannot remove source review protection. Approved proposals preserve exact candidate/reviewer/preview fences but create a fresh linked run. Explicit revision publication and its operation commit before default supersession. Admission checks exact inputs/kinds, capacity, interpolation, and starter authority before cancellation. Each writer handles at most 32 sources from one head using indexed capacity facts. Pending sources cannot admit new work claims, activation, program credentials, or owned/mechanical-gate starts; recorded refusals release that hold. Terminal state or cleanup expiry cannot release a replacement before ancestor/descendant runtime quiescence and effective program fencing. Every host-initiated or explicit termination is retained before its outcome is reported and awaits actual worker exit, not merely Worker.terminate(). Exact host/step/attempt identities survive removal from running state and same-step replacement. Daemon failure removes running state and registers cancellation under one mutex; worker-message forwarding excludes host lifecycle notifications. Pending worker and effect-group fences are scoped to this supersession lineage, including descendants across every generation, so unrelated cancellations do not hold admission or finalizers. Liveness failure remains immediately visible while native worker exit is pending. No new DSL grammar, authority grant, policy knob, retry, or timeout is introduced.

compatibility.detail: Coordinate participating member upgrades before upgraded owners process stale active runs or new publications, because registry and retention digests change. Upgrade the daemon and its bundled program host together: all termination paths now send ending before terminal notifications, then an attempt- and host-incarnation-qualified cancelled acknowledgement after actual worker exit. Supersession admission also requires recorded effect-group fencing within its own lineage. Startup recovery respects existing review/idle policy. Older tolerant clients ignore additive fields; new clients accept older responses. Unreviewed direct generation adoption remains available; approved proposal responses name the fresh replacement, not the source. A deliberate same-revision retry after publication remains pinned until a later different definition is published.

downtime.detail: No fleet shutdown or destructive data migration is required. Default publication supersession or approved cutover intentionally cancels an eligible source only after admission succeeds, then waits for ordinary cleanup and confirmed runtime/effect fencing before replacement work. Cleanup expiry does not waive this hold, and waiting does not spend the replacement timeout. When-idle policy waits for current work; human-only policy waits for approval. A replacement admission refusal leaves the source active.

manual.detail: Review fresh-start compatibility before publishing and keep existing review/idle policies where intended; automatic S3 is the default, not an override of those policies. Human-only publication still needs the normal person-approved proposal. Make all steps and program effects idempotent against prior effects. Inspect missions show or public readers for supersedes, superseded_by, supersession_fault, and revision-draining idle holds. Republishing the same revision alone does nothing.

recovery.detail: Supersession does not undo effects or erase history. For admission failure inspect both revisions and supersession_fault, correct the definition, and publish a new revision; refusal releases an automatic idle hold. cleanup-runtime-quiescence and supersession-runtime-quiescence faults require confirmation that the exact owned runtime incarnation ended, not a stale stop or unreachable report. supersession-effect-fence requires matching host termination acknowledgements or host exit plus verified leftover-group fencing for this lineage, not unrelated cancellations; uncertain process identity or kill failure remains blocked. A failed step or removed running entry is not worker-exit proof. Observations and acknowledgements wake recovery without polling. Stop new supersession writes before downgrade, retain durable history, and use a compatible owner/reader for in-flight revision-draining or supersession-waiting histories.
